title: Admin-initiated session revocation and audit context for SAML-provisioned RBAC v2
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Admins need a reliable way to immediately revoke sessions that were created via SAML JIT provisioning while preserving an auditable trail that ties the revocation event back to the original assertion and RBAC v2 role mapping. Current gaps: runtime session keys aren't correlated with audit events, admin-initiated revocations sometimes leave active streaming connections open, and the system cannot distinguish sessions provisioned without MFA from those with step-up performed later.

Goal: Implement a revocation flow that: (1) attaches an immutable audit_correlation_id to sessions at SAML assertion time, (2) persists auth metadata (auth_time, acr/loa, assertion_id, mapped_roles) in the session store, (3) allows admins to revoke at user, role, or session-id granularity via Console/API, and (4) ensures immediate enforcement in the serving runtime with guaranteed audit-log entries for every action. This must work with RBAC v2 role bindings and include sensible grace behavior for in-flight streaming responses.

Scope: server-side session lifecycle (authn layer + session store), Console admin controls (UI + backend), runtime eviction hooks, audit log enrichment, and migration of existing sessions to include audit_correlation_id. Not in scope: SAML IdP changes beyond recommended assertion claims, long-term archival retention policy decisions (handled by compliance).
updates: 2026-02-10: Triage - Security flagged multiple customer requests for immediate admin logout and forensics traceability. Assigned to Liam. References: security post-mortem SEC-2026-01-11.

2026-02-14: Design sync - Decided to generate audit_correlation_id at assertion intake and include it in session footprint. Use existing session-store schema extension (small, backward-compatible JSON blob). Trade-off: slightly larger session records vs. reliable post-hoc tracing.

2026-02-18: Prototype - Runtime eviction added via pub/sub channel 'session-revoke-v2' to push session_id/audit_correlation_id to serving nodes. Implemented soft-close: allow in-flight token generation to finish, then block new tokens for revoked session IDs. Noted streaming edge-case: long-lived SSEs will be terminated with 410 after graceful drain (30s).

2026-02-22: Security review - Requested explicit handling of missing 'acr' (MFA claim). Chosen behavior: treat absent acr as 'unknown' and require admin-visible flag; do not auto-step-up. Recorded decision in Confluence page.

2026-02-25: PR opened - GitHub PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6723 includes session-store schema, Console API endpoints, and runtime eviction listener. Marked as draft while adding audit plumbing.

2026-03-01: Integration tests - End-to-end test created that: provisions user via SAML JIT with acr=urn:mfa:webauthn, maps role editor -> rbac v2 binding, issues session, admin revokes session, asserts serving node rejects subsequent requests and audit log contains correlation_id + assertion_id. Tests flaky in CI due to timing; retry logic added.
acceptance_criteria: Sessions created from SAML JIT contain audit_correlation_id and stored fields: assertion_id, issuer, auth_time, acr, mapped_roles
Admin can revoke by session_id, user_id, or role_binding_id via Console and API; revocation triggers runtime eviction within 10s under normal load
Serving runtime rejects new requests for revoked sessions and terminates streaming connections with 410 after 30s drain; in-flight token generations complete but subsequent chunks are blocked
Every revocation action emits an audit log entry with correlation_id, admin_actor, revocation_reason, and affected session_ids; audit records are visible in Console and exportable to SIEM
Migration script converts existing sessions to include audit_correlation_id without downtime; rollforward strategy documented
End-to-end tests cover happy path, missing acr handling, and role-scoped revocation
work_items: Add audit_correlation_id and assertion metadata to session-store schema (platform/session-store)
Console: add 'Force logout' button on user and role pages; backend API endpoint POST /admin/sessions/revoke
Runtime: subscribe to 'session-revoke-v2' topic and evict matching session_ids / correlation_ids
Audit: enrich existing audit pipeline to include correlation_id in all session lifecycle events
Migration: backfill correlation_id for active sessions with non-destructive rollout
Tests: integration + chaos tests for eviction under load and streaming behavior
risks: Race between revocation and ongoing token generation may allow one extra token; mitigated by soft-close and short drain window
Large-scale revocations (org-wide) could create a spike in eviction messages; mitigation: batch invalidation and progressive rollout policy
Missing or untrusted 'acr' claims from some IdPs require conservative handling to avoid accidentally weakening MFA posture
Audit log volume increase and costs - finance sign-off may be required for longer retention during incident investigations
